Start With Five

Everything said and found about Denver onboarding, in one place. What you and Olivia agreed, what the app does today, what other apps do, and a flow you can click through before Friday.

For Julia and Olivia. Written Nov 18, 2026, after today’s call. From five call transcripts (Nov 2 to Nov 18), your Slack thread, the shared board, a read of the mobile app and backend code as of today, and 16 App Store screens from 11 apps that I checked one by one.

The short version

What is already agreed

The first build is onboarding: bring your recs in easily, then choose your Denver Top 5. Ask Denver comes after. Top 5 is open to everyone in Denver, not only ambassadors. You show a prototype on your phone at the dinner. Nothing big gets built on background location. Agreed Nov 12 and Nov 18

Today’s sign-up is 20 screens, built for creators

Phone, email, password, name, permissions, invite code, username, photo, bio, socials, friends, “Join 500K+ Creators”, brand partners, 3 product recs, 3 local recs, a badge, share for $5, welcome. Nothing knows about Denver. There is no city pick and no taste pick. Found in the mobile app

A Denver path: 9 creator screens become 4 steps

Arrive through an ambassador’s link, bring your Denver, keep what is right, pick your Top 5. Then one shared taste and a card to post. Sign-in screens stay as they are. Every new screen gives the person something back. Proposed

What two dev days can hold

A short Denver branch of sign-up, plus a Top 5 list that shows first on the profile. Both reuse what exists: the local add-rec loop already fills a list called “My top {City} recs”, and invite codes can already tag who came from whom. Proposed

Shared Tastes cannot ship by Dec 1. Today every manual add makes a new copy of the place, so the app cannot tell that you and Maya picked the same Hop Alley. That fix goes in Dec 2 to 11. Found

This week, with no engineering

Olivia asks each ambassador and the Denver creators already on Benable for their Top 5 by text. Entered by hand, that fills the “places Denver loves” grid, gives new people someone to match with on day one, and is the first ambassador assignment Olivia already suggested. about 18 ambassadors × 5 = 90 picks (18 is the middle of Olivia’s 15 to 20) Proposed

The dinner is Tony’s test

On Nov 2 he asked to put fake prototypes in front of about three Denver creators before building. The phone prototype at the dinner does that, and the Dec 2 to 11 build can follow what you see them do. Proposed

Both can be true if “live” means the short Denver path and the Top 5 list, and the dinner shows the rest on your phone. Settle what “live by Dec 2” means on Friday, before Tony asks on Monday.

The Top 5 is already half there

The local part of today’s sign-up asks for a favorite restaurant, park and coffee shop near your city, up to 3, and puts them in an auto-made list called “My top {City} recs”. Raising 3 to 5, fixing the city to Denver and showing that list first is most of a Top 5. Found

Where: features/onboarding/sign-up/add-rec/note/screen.tsx, lines 146 to 160 and 338 to 340.

Ambassador tagging needs a data row, not code

Every user already has a reusable invite code. A code can carry a user type, and people who sign up with it get that tag. The app already reads the code from AppsFlyer links. An “ambassador” type on each ambassador’s code tags everyone they bring in. Found

Where: user_type_app_invites, user_service.rb lines 20 to 34; mobile hooks/rootLayout/appsFlyer.ts.

Top Obsessions was real, and web only

Nisarg built it Dec 2025 to Jan 2026: a public page with a reveal, emoji reactions and email capture, made by admins only. Its items are free text, not places, and there is no screen in the app. The reveal and reactions are worth keeping. The data is not. Found

Where: app/models/obsession.rb; benable-ui Obsession.svelte.

Import parts exist, unconnected

The share sheet works today: share any link to Benable and it becomes a rec through autofill, with no TikTok or Maps-specific handling. The TikTok importer runs on the server but the app never calls it. There is still no Google Maps import of any kind. Found

Where: shareExtension/; /api/tiktok_importer.

The Denver flow, screen by screen

Sam is new in Denver and taps Maya’s link. Tap places on the keep and Top 5 screens; the buttons that save or follow work too.

Same Denver base as the chats and feed studies: the g40 map, the same 14 real Denver places, placeholder people. Map crops stand in for photos. Every caption says whether the screen is agreed or only proposed.

Why the steps are in this order

Bring, keep, pick is the order Olivia described on Nov 6: people cannot name places cold, so give them a list first and let them choose from it. The Top 5 comes third because it is picked from what was just kept, which none of the 13 apps I studied does. The shared taste comes after the Top 5 because the Top 5 is where a match is most likely: 18 ambassadors × 5 picks = 90 places already in someone’s Top 5. The card comes last so onboarding ends on something worth posting.

Shared Tastes needs one fix first

The moment is simple: you add Hop Alley, and the app says Maya recs it too. The app cannot do that yet.

What is in the way

When you add a place by hand or in onboarding, the backend saves a brand new copy of that place for your rec. The app looks up a Google place ID only when you edit an address, and never sends it. So two people who both rec Hop Alley have two unrelated Hop Alleys. Only recs made from background location carry a real Google ID. Found

The fix

Give every new Denver place rec a Google place ID when it is saved, and backfill the Denver recs that exist. Then one endpoint: who else recs this place. Discover already has the same shape for products, “other creators who recommend the same product”, built in October, so the screen and API pattern exist. Proposed

Show a count, not a percentage

Beli’s match score and Spotify Blend’s percentage both need history a new person does not have. Corner shows “45 in common” with two faces, which works from the first overlap. Start there: “Maya recs Hop Alley too”, then “3 more Denver people share 2 of your places”. Proposed

Seed it so nobody gets nothing

A new person only sees a match if someone already recs their place. Ambassadors’ Top 5s collected this week cover up to 18 × 5 = 90 picks, fewer once they overlap, and the overlaps are the point. If a pick has no match, show the ambassadors who rec places nearby, the way Timeleft shows the people waiting before you meet them. Proposed

Not checked: how many existing Denver recs already have a Google ID, and whether Discover’s matching covers places as well as products. One query and one question to Nisarg settle both.

How others do it

11 apps, 16 screens. Store screenshots are marketing screens the company published, not onboarding captures, and none shows a first-run picker, so the onboarding steps themselves are described from articles.

80%+

of Beli users joined through a referral. Ivey Business Review

4 invites

Beli makes you send before you can sign up. Friends replied “Were you hacked?”. Demand Curve

8×

more likely to swap numbers with Hinge’s single daily Most Compatible pick, in Hinge’s own early test. TechCrunch

“a lifeboat”

Letterboxd’s head of social on why Four Favorites stops at four: one slot more and it loses its stakes. The Spinoff

A Top N that looks like you

Short, at the top of the profile, with something that reads the person.

The first “someone like you”

Per place, with a reason, before there is enough data for a score.

Arriving, by city

The city is a label everywhere, and other people are visible before you do anything.

Twelve rules this adds up to

  1. Build the Top 5 from what they just brought in, with search as the fallback.
  2. Keep it at 5. Show empty slots as gaps, so the profile asks to be finished.
  3. Put the Top 5 at the very top of the profile.
  4. One line under the five that reads the person, like StoryGraph’s.
  5. End onboarding on a card worth posting.
  6. Show the first shared taste the first time it exists: one person, their note.
  1. Always say why: “Maya recs Hop Alley too.”
  2. Make sure ambassadors’ picks cover the places new people will name.
  3. Ambassador links, not a forced invite gate.
  4. No location ask in onboarding. The link or a pick says Denver.
  5. If there is a Want to Try, fill it from a short checklist.
  6. Ask Denver is a card after onboarding, not a step in it.

All twelve Proposed.
